conventions.convention: e is a finite integer ≥2, I=Z/eZ, q is indeterminate over Q, and every q_i=q. At e=2 the off-diagonal Cartan entries are −2. The full weight datum includes independent simple roots, δ=sum α_i, and the degree direction d.

u_m=z^a v_j when m=j−ae, with 1≤j≤e and j=e representing residue 0. Its weight is Λ_j−Λ_(j−1)+aδ. Normal wedge order is decreasing integer index. The opposite-channel energy is χ(j>k)+b−a and is positive exactly for decreasing indices.
The fixed coproduct is ΔE_i=E_i⊗K_i⁻¹+1⊗E_i and ΔF_i=F_i⊗1+K_i⊗F_i. The Hecke normalization is Q=q², S_i²=(Q−1)S_i+Q, t_i=−q⁻¹S_i, and A_N=sum S_w. Hecke products act on the left.

The charge-M vacuum is u_M∧u_(M−1)∧…, and partition indices are i_k=M+λ_k−k+1. Ω_0=Λ_0 and Ω_M−Ω_(M−1)=wt(u_M). The separated topology uses q^nF_0 with A_0=Q[q]_(q), not the Laurent lattice F_A, on which q is a unit.

At charge 0 a cell in row r, column c has residue c−r modulo e and partition weight Λ_0−sum m_iα_i. Regular means every positive part has multiplicity <e; restricted means every adjacent row difference is <e.

Boundary nodes are ordered by increasing content. F_i coefficients count signed same-residue corners strictly to the right; E_i coefficients count strictly to the left in the smaller diagram and negate that count. The chosen node is excluded.

In increasing content order, + denotes addable and − removable. Cancel adjacent −+ pairs; the first surviving − is good for deletion and the last surviving + is cogood for addition. These are normalized Kashiwara arrows, not Chevalley coefficient minimizers.

The general highest-weight decomposition assumes AC. The full Fock crystal contains all partitions, while the vacuum component has regular labels. Highest crystal vertices need not be highest standard field vectors.

Lower-basis columns expand in standard partition rows, with corrections on strictly dominated partitions in qZ[q]. Exactly regular columns belong to the basic lower global basis. The transpose-conjugation symmetry asserted for the bar matrix is not a symmetry of the lower coefficient matrix.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer e≥2, the displayed cyclic Cartan matrix, free lattices P and P∨, perfect pairing, independent simple roots, central element and normalized affine weight form define the stated affine type-A datum; sum α_i=δ and every root has level 0.

A_NS_i=S_iA_N=q²A_N, A_N²=C_NA_N with C_N≠0, and ker A_N=sum_i ker(S_i+1). The quotient is isomorphic to im A_N as a quantum-group module, and the complete two-factor Laurent kernel gives the displayed straightening relations.

For every N≥1, strictly decreasing-index wedges form a Q(q)-basis of W_N and an A-basis of W_A. Straightening terminates by the finite dominance/inversion profile, and the separate local chart L_0=A_0W_0 has the ordered-wedge crystal basis.

Normal semi-infinite wedges are indexed by partitions through i_k=M+λ_k−k+1. Stable finite-prefix action gives the finite node sums with coefficients q^(A_i^r−R_i^r) for F_i and q^−(A_i^l−R_i^l) for E_i, and the stated normalized toral actions.

For each fixed residue, the toggle orbit is a finite Boolean cube, including e=2; its node operators equal the fixed-coproduct tensor power of highest-weight-one strings. The actual normalized operators preserve the raw A_0 partition span and obey the signature-survivor rule; divided powers have Laurent-integral matrices.

On the chosen integral-label-graded B-module W, the toral and toral-action relations, mixed commutators and local nilpotence of every E_i and F_i imply both quantum Serre families as operator identities, including the e=2 cubic sums; no Serre relation is assumed.

The constructed node operators on all charge-0 partition vectors make F a chosen P-graded integrable U_q(affine sl_e)-module: every toral rule, mixed commutator and both Serre sums hold, including e=2.

Assuming the declared AC, the empty component is B(Λ_0), with exactly the e-regular labels; its module is M=U_q|empty⟩ and its lower lattice is M∩F_0. It occurs once, and F is the locally weight-finite direct sum of V(Λ_0−kδ) with multiplicities p(k).

The explicit vacuum-fixed wedge bar has a unique integral triangular correction G(λ)=|λ⟩+sum d_(μ,λ)(q)|μ⟩ on strictly dominated shapes, with d in qZ[q] and same-core support. The full family bases F_A and F_0, and exactly its regular members form the lower global basis of M.

concerns.concern: F3, line 60, says the module 'decomposes canonically into a locally weight-finite direct sum of highest weight crystals and their modules'. The cited decomposition theorem's Statement (ii), line 38, asserts existence of an isomorphism Φ and uniqueness of the constituent multiset; its Choice paragraph, line 42, explicitly allows choices of summands and residue lifts. Canonical crystal components should be distinguished from a canonical field-module splitting. The proof here needs only existence and multiplicities, so this is wording rather than a defect in the displayed decomposition.

seams_checked.note: The tensor-rule tie conventions, finite-weight/cone hypotheses and AC assumption are preserved. One wording overstatement remains: the empty-component theorem's F3 calls the field decomposition canonical, whereas the supplier asserts an isomorphism and a unique constituent multiset with choices of lifts. See the presentation concern.

The Fock theorem constructs its own bar and ambient balanced charts, then uses the highest-module lower-basis existence and uniqueness only for M. It preserves the distinction between lower integral lattices and form-dual upper coordinates.

The bridge explicitly transports by JM_λ=|λ′⟩ with q unchanged and colors reflected. It preserves signature polarity, regular/restricted label sets, the full-versus-basic distinction, decomposition assumptions and the direction of lower-basis triangularity.

This is an affine/level-one context prerequisite. The page's items do not directly cite the assigned Fock suppliers, and the page does not infer arbitrary-weight categorification or global-basis claims from the level-one construction.

Direct uses are of the cyclic datum: finite residue labels, dominant coroot multiplicities, normalized weight-root pairing and the e=2 double edge. Hecke parameters and grading variables remain distinct, and e=0 is explicitly outside the cyclic scope.

The consumers preserve the normalized affine form and node action. Their standard Specht images are projected coordinate functionals in the basic upper dual lattice; they do not identify all raw partition vectors with a basis of the basic module or confuse its upper Gram coordinates with lower coefficients.
